concept.label: SQL Concept Lab
concept.description: A small browser-local database for fast SQL concept retrieval. It is intentionally independent from the course-faithful University database.

exercises.prompt: List every student name in alphabetical order.
exercises.starter: SELECT name FROM Student ORDER BY name;
exercises.explanation: Select one column and make ordering explicit.

exercises.prompt: Return each student with the department name.
exercises.starter:
SELECT s.name, d.name AS department
FROM Student s
JOIN Department d ON d.id = s.department_id
ORDER BY s.id;
exercises.explanation: The join uses Student.department_id to Department.id.

exercises.prompt: Find departments with at least two students.
exercises.starter:
SELECT d.name, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM Department d
JOIN Student s ON s.department_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
exercises.explanation: HAVING filters the aggregate result after GROUP BY.

exercises.prompt: Which key pair prevents duplicate enrollments for one student and course?
exercises.starter: -- Write the constraint in words or SQL
exercises.explanation: The composite key identifies one enrollment per student-course pair.

mysql.label: DSA5104 MySQL Lab
mysql.description: The course-faithful practice mode uses the canonical University schema and MySQL-compatible query prompts. Atlas prefers the configured server-side MySQL runner; when it is unavailable, the same University data runs in SQLite/WASM as an explicitly labelled compatibility fallback.

schema.name: teaches
columns: PRIMARY KEY (ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year)

schema.name: takes
columns: PRIMARY KEY (ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year)

exercises.prompt: List all department names in alphabetical order.
exercises.explanation: This is a real University relation, not the concept-lab toy schema.

exercises.prompt: List every Computer Science course by course id.
exercises.starter:
SELECT course_id, title
FROM course
WHERE dept_name = 'Comp. Sci.'
ORDER BY course_id;
exercises.explanation: Use the University column names exactly: course.dept_name and course.course_id.

exercises.prompt: Find instructors who teach no section, while keeping the unmatched instructor rows.
exercises.starter:
SELECT i.ID, i.name
FROM instructor AS i
LEFT JOIN teaches AS t ON t.ID = i.ID
WHERE t.ID IS NULL
ORDER BY i.ID;
exercises.explanation: The LEFT JOIN preserves instructors before the NULL test removes matched teaching rows.

exercises.prompt: Count courses offered by each department.
exercises.starter:
SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS course_count
FROM course
GROUP BY dept_name
ORDER BY dept_name;
exercises.explanation: Every non-aggregate selected column belongs in GROUP BY for portable MySQL semantics.

exercises.prompt: Return the three highest-paid instructors using MySQL LIMIT.
exercises.starter:
SELECT ID, name
FROM instructor
ORDER BY salary DESC
LIMIT 3;
exercises.explanation: LIMIT is a MySQL-compatible way to express a top-k result after ordering.

exercises.prompt: Show each advised student together with the advisor name.
exercises.starter:
SELECT s.name AS student, i.name AS advisor
FROM student AS s
JOIN advisor AS a ON a.s_ID = s.ID
JOIN instructor AS i ON i.ID = a.i_ID
ORDER BY s.ID;
exercises.explanation: Follow the foreign-key path from student, then advisor, then instructor rather than joining on department names.

exercises.prompt: Write a transaction that changes one row and then proves ROLLBACK restores it.
exercises.explanation: The MySQL lab teaches transaction syntax as a controlled server-side action; the browser fallback does not persist mutations.
